items.description: A busy market in Yaounde where traders sell food, clothes, and daily goods. It reflects the capital's everyday urban life.
A coffee farm in the Bamenda area. It shows the role of highland agriculture in the local economy.
A cattle ranch near Ngaoundere on the Adamawa plateau. Livestock farming is a major part of the regional way of life.
River fishing along the Benue near Garoua. It remains an important source of food and income for local families.
A cocoa garden near Ebolowa in the south. Cocoa farming is a core part of the area's rural economy.
A craft market in Foumban where artisans sell carvings, metalwork, and pottery. It connects local production with visitors.
A museum park in Dschang that combines open space with local heritage displays. It is a calm place for learning and walks.
A fish market in Kribi close to the coast. It is a daily meeting point for fishers, traders, and buyers.
A maize field in the Bafoussam area. It reflects the importance of staple crop farming in the western highlands.
A forest honey site near Bertoua in the east. Honey gathering is part of local small-scale rural production.
A wildlife reserve area in the Mbam region. It supports animal viewing and nature-based local activity.
A museum garden in Bamenda that mixes local plants with cultural displays. It is used for quiet visits and education.
A rainforest area near Djoum in southern Cameroon. It reflects the forest-based way of life in the south.
A cocoa cooperative near Sangmelima. It helps small farmers organize production and market their harvests.
A vegetable market in Foumbot where local growers sell fresh produce. It is part of the town's daily food supply.
